clue.text: Keelhauling is putting a man under this?

definitions.text: Keelhauling is putting a man under this?

parts.words: Keelhauling is putting a man under this?
parts.note: keelhauling literally drags a sailor beneath the keel of a vessel, so the punishment is read as a man put under a tough boat; the everyday sense is severe suffering

explanation.surface: A grim question about the old naval punishment of dragging a sailor under the keel.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as HARD SHIP: a man keelhauled is put under a ship, and the ordeal is certainly a severe privation.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelhauling was a brutal punishment, the very picture of severe suffering and privation.

clue.text: Familiar need for a newborn

definitions.meaning: familiar with, up to date, as in keeping up with the news
read as two words, a mother's breast, what a baby needs to feed

explanation.surface: A familiar requirement of any newborn baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer split as A BREAST for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up with the latest is to be well informed and familiar; a newborn needs a breast to feed.

clue.text: Short period inside expired, so driven away

indicators.note: the period sits within the word for expired

parts.note: died means expired
a spell is a short period of time

explanation.surface: A brief time ran out, so someone was chased off.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts or crowds that are dispersed or banished have been sent away.

clue.text: Composer raising money for title

indicators.note: in a down clue the money letter is lifted higher up the column

parts.note: Handel was the German-born composer of Messiah
L stands for pounds, money

explanation.surface: A composer raising cash for a title.
explanation.walkthrough: In the down entry L moves up, from after E to before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name or title, as in a handle to one's name.

clue.text: Work harder to raise levels over a couple of feet

definitions.meaning: an idiom for making more effort

definitions.text: to raise levels over a couple of feet
definitions.meaning: literally hoisting hosiery up over two feet

explanation.surface: Instructions to work harder, like hitching up hosiery over both feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is read literally: hauling the hosiery on one's two feet up higher.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a greater effort or improve one's performance.

clue.text: Fairy at risk from Puck's broom?

definitions.meaning: one of Titania's attendant fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream bears this name
Puck enters at the play's end with a broom to sweep the dust behind the door, so a spider's silky trap would be swept away

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean sprite fears being swept up by the mischievous Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves come from A Midsummer Night's Dream: a fairy of Titania's train, and the dusty threads Puck's broom would clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaseblossom, Moth, Mustardseed and this one are Titania's fairies; Puck's sweeping would clear away spider silk.

clue.text: Hat blown off in wind ranging far and wide

indicators.note: the jumbled hat goes inside the word for wind

parts.note: colic is pain from wind in the gut

indicators.note: a hat blown off by the wind is tossed about, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hat whipped away by a gust, carried far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like the weather that blew the hat away, but here it is the stomach complaint; 'blown off' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic tastes are universal and wide-ranging.

clue.text: A little fine weather for this time of the year

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, as in not a whit
sun is fine weather

explanation.surface: Hoping for a spot of sunshine at this season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of Pentecost and its season fall seven weeks after Easter.

clue.text: Entrance into artistic show reduced — it's of little value

indicators.note: the entrance goes inside the shortened show
the show loses its final letter, cut down in length

parts.note: a ballet is an artistic performance
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Admission to an arts performance cut to a trifling price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' drops the show's last letter, and 'into' puts the entrance inside what remains, near the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a trifle, something unimportant.

clue.text: Cooler sort of house, where shades may close on boy

definitions.meaning: cooler is slang for a jail

definitions.text: sort of house, where shades may close on boy
definitions.meaning: Wordsworth's Intimations ode says shades of the ...-house begin to close upon the growing boy

explanation.surface: A chilly description of a gloomy house where darkness gathers round a child.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half quotes Wordsworth: 'Shades of the prison-house begin to close / Upon the growing Boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail, a place of confinement.

clue.text: Securing French and English articles, having inserted key

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article

indicators.note: the article phrase has something put into it, so these words signal one piece going inside another

parts.note: an article in plain English is a thing, an object
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: A grammatical note on articles in two languages, as if keying in an entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' works in two senses: the grammatical article in French, and the everyday English meaning of an object. 'Having inserted' puts the musical key inside the second of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Latching a door means fastening or making it secure.

clue.text: Look round on river where Etonian sportsmen were successful

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the look-and-round piece comes after the river

parts.note: water is used in place names for a river or stream, as in Derwent Water's feeder becks
lo is an old word meaning look
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone glances about by a river where Eton's athletes won glory.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying that the Battle of Waterloo was won on the playing fields of Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington supposedly said the battle against Napoleon was won on Eton's playing fields, so its old boys triumphed there.

clue.text: Kickoff given in error to team

parts.note: a guess that is wrong is said to be out
a set is a group playing together, as in tennis doubles or a dance

explanation.surface: A football kickoff awarded to a team by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The kickoff is the very start of a match, so it means the beginning.

clue.text: Country I reckon has only one lake

indicators.note: the word for reckon is allowed only a single lake, so one of its two lake letters is dropped

parts.note: to tally is to count up or reckon
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone reckons a whole country contains just a single lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for reckon has a double lake letter; 'has only one lake' strips one of the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A European nation whose capital is Rome.

clue.text: I heavily criticize a wicked city

parts.note: to slam is to criticize harshly
bad means wicked

explanation.surface: Someone harshly condemns an evil city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Pakistan.

clue.text: Not quite fit to appear in important cup-tie

definitions.text: Not quite fit to appear in important cup-tie

parts.words: Not quite fit to appear in important cup-tie
parts.note: a team that is not quite good enough to reach the final falls one round short, in the round before it

explanation.surface: A footballer, still carrying a knock, may miss a big knockout match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an injured player; the cryptic reading is the round that falls just short of the final, 'not quite' hinting at semi.
explanation.definitionFit: The penultimate round of a knockout cup decides who reaches the final.

clue.text: Not even unusually rare girl secures university entrance

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the next piece fast within them
the letters are arranged in an unusual order
the entrance of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An exceptional girl wins a place at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' is the definition, not a hint at odd letters; 'unusually' scrambles the two words and 'secures' holds the university's opening letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven or not uniform is erratic and inconsistent.

clue.text: Depend on comparatively little, being endlessly active

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: rest on means depend on
less is the comparative of little

explanation.surface: Relying on less and less, one is forever on the go.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to keep still is constantly in motion.

clue.text: American wartime scheme arranged to supply all English needs?

indicators.note: the letters are set out in a new arrangement to form the scheme's name

explanation.surface: A US wartime programme set up to meet every British requirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' shuffles ALL, E and NEEDS. The surface fits: the scheme did supply Britain's needs.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1941 US programme supplied Britain and other Allies with arms and materials during the Second World War.

clue.text: Emma's married name pronounced at regular intervals

indicators.note: the surname is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: in Jane Austen's Emma, the heroine marries Mr Knightley

explanation.surface: How the heroine's new surname is said at set intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Woodhouse marries George Knightley in Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every night occurs at regular intervals.

clue.text: Conspire to incriminate, using piece of film

definitions.meaning: to fit up an innocent person with false evidence
a single exposure on a strip of cinema film

explanation.surface: A plot to fit someone up using a snippet of footage as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up an innocent person is to fit them up; a single still on a reel is one picture of the sequence.

clue.text: Tiny sound finally included in record

parts.note: minute means tiny

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word sound

explanation.surface: A tiny sound at the end is captured on a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A point formally noted in a meeting's official record has been minuted.

clue.text: Family doctor got inside old robe

indicators.note: the doctor enters the family word

parts.note: kin are one's family
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A family doctor slips into an old dressing gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose wide-sleeved Japanese gown.

clue.text: Publication persuaded young to fly

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
got, as in got him to agree, means persuaded

explanation.surface: A magazine article coaxed a youngster to take a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young to fly' reads like a child persuaded onto a plane, but it means the offspring of a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young stage of a fly before it pupates.

clue.text: Showing fear of cold calling

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
ringing someone means calling them on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone dreads cold calling on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch and cower is to display fear or servility.

clue.text: Reinforce bar with lock

parts.note: bar meaning except is but, as in all but one
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Strengthening a door with a bar and a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up or support a wall or argument is to strengthen it.

clue.text: Dedicated person able to undergo conversion

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: A devout believer is capable of a religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undergo conversion' rearranges ABLE TO; the religious surface fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay person devoted to a monastery or religious life, offered to God's service.

clue.text: Senior people showing desire to break into computer system

indicators.note: one piece forces its way inside the other, as a hacker breaks into a system

parts.note: DOS is a disk operating system for computers
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Elder figures reveal an urge to hack a computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: The most respected or longest-serving members of a group are its elders.

clue.text: Stick out for right to keep daughter

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: the word for right holds the next piece inside it, as one keeps something

parts.note: true means right or correct

explanation.surface: A parent holds out for the right to keep custody of their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To jut or project beyond a surface.
